title: A download workbook that a program never finishes is neither logged nor cut off when the program returns.
text: `rule:core-classes/spreadsheet-writes-as-a-stream` says a workbook never finished is logged as an error naming its target when the request ends, and a download is cut off. A program that throws, meets a limit or is cancelled mid-download is cut off: `nvs_host`'s isolate `finish` aborts the request's body stream, and the server ends the response in an error frame (`crates/nvs-host/src/isolate.rs`, `nvs_runtime::stream::Emit::abort`). A program that returns normally with the workbook unfinished ends its body cleanly, because `Workbook` registers nothing that runs at the request's end: its `finished` flag is read only by its own members (`extensions/spreadsheet/nvs/Workbook.nvs`). The browser then saves a broken file and nothing is logged. No Novis method can abort a response body today. The user decided the fix: `Core\Response::stream` takes an option that marks the stream as one that must be finished, with a label for the log, and `Core\Response\Stream` gets an `end()` method. When the request ends, the host logs a marked stream that was not ended as an error naming its label, and cuts its body off with an error frame (`nvs_runtime::stream::Emit::abort`), so no user code runs at the request's end (`rule:concurrency/cancellation-runs-no-user-code`). `Workbook::createForDownload` marks its stream with the download's name, and `finish` ends it. It costs one flag per stream; the option's name is settled in the rule that ships it. A request-end hook with `Stream::abort()` was declined because it runs user code after the handler returns, and dropping the promise because the browser would save a broken file.
